findings.finding: Opens 'We did not replicate three of the four simulation headlines of Chen (2021), who reported biased direct-effect estimates, percentile bootstrap intervals that cover the true value far too rarely, and power for the mediated interaction (MINT) near zero.' Verdict, cited source (\citet{chen2021}, verified against the title page: Donna Chen, Univ. of Nebraska-Lincoln, Dec 2021) and the original findings in one sentence.

Signed headline numbers follow (85.42% vs 0.00%; 43.62 vs 0.04 points; 0.013 (raw 0.063) vs 0.802 (raw 0.852)), then the fourth headline 'holds in part', then the evidence limit (Head Start not rerunnable). Order matches manuscript.md.

Polish: 'Her figures instead match results from data without the treatment-by-mediator interaction, and her coverage a comparison with population values wrong for treated cases; the rule behind her bias is not determined; ...' is elliptical and a three-semicolon chain.

Opens with the same verdict and numbers (Table 4.8 85.42% vs 0.00%; coverage 24.10-83.99% vs 94.6-95.6%; MINT 0.063 vs 0.852, i.e. 0.013 vs 0.802), then MC SEs, the H4 partial result, the evidence limit and 'No estimate reverses its sign.'
Tolerances restated (half a printed unit; figure reading error) and 'not tests of equivalence'.
Polish: uses the label 'S9' before any S-label is defined (defined only in Appendix C, p. 23).
Readable without the research conversation; no references to drafts, reviews or internal roles.
Process narration (who was asked when; 'research workspace') is kept because it documents a consequential departure from the source's software; acceptable, polish only.
Polish: S1-S9 labels are used from p. 2 but defined only in Appendix C (p. 23).
No commit hash or working branch named; 'those on the master branch, where every link points'. commit_refs.py accepted the source (no errors); stage_checks.py cues returned no cue IDs.

Published effect 85.42 = mean over six Table 4.8 PNDE/TNDE rows of (100 - within[-.10,.10]) = 85.4167 (source-values/table_4_8.csv; source PDF p. 102). Ours 0.00 (results/table48_ours.csv within_10 = 100 for all six rows). Tolerance 0.005 correct for a mean of 2-decimal values. 'smaller', 'zero vs nonzero' correct (0.00 within tolerance of zero).

Published 43.62 = 95 - mean Table 4.9 coverage 51.381 (43.619; PDF p. 138). Ours 0.04 = 95 - 94.9642 = 0.0358 (results/table49_ours.csv). Tolerance 0.005. 'smaller', 'same direction' per contract; MC SE 0.005/0.019 stated in Section 1 (results/mc_se_headline.json).
Published 47.07 (computed 47.0713), ours 0.33 (computed 0.3258); tolerance 0.01 = two weighted half-units; labels correct.

Published 0.013 = mean(.0683, .0571) - .05 = 0.0127 (results/digitized_rates.csv rows 4.28 MINT n=500 a=.59 h=.34 cut 2-3, status read; Figure 4.28 inspected on source PDF p. 136). Ours 0.802 = 0.8518 - .05 (results/cells.csv, 32 cells). Tolerance 0.0091 = mean of per-point reading errors .0052 and .0131 (=.00915), rounded down, kind measurement, disclosed as post hoc (caption; Section 7.5). 0.0127 > 0.0091 so 'same direction' follows the contract; 'larger' correct.
Nonscalar H4: scalar columns 'not established', tolerance not applicable, verdict 'partial' matches packet status partly_replicated.
All 13 packet claims (H1-H4, S1-S9) appear with statuses matching the packet: H1-H3 and S1 not replicated, H4/S2/S3/S9 partly, S4/S6 blocked, S5 replicated, S7/S8 not established.
Every claim has a row; numerical/scope labels match packet numerical and reconstruction fields (S5 'match'; S4/S6 'withheld'/'unavailable'; S8 'not applicable').

S2 13/18 (14 slack), S3 16/28 (17 slack), 29/46 and 31/46, 39/46 with h=0, the 7 residual statements {2,43,10,11,30,41,44}, S5 24+24 and S9 10/15 all recomputed from results/statement_checks.csv, secondary/table_arithmetic.csv and results/significance_conclusions.json.

S8 handled as not established with the stated search terms; nothing blocked is called a nonreplication (S4, S6 'not established, and not a failure to replicate', p. 8). claim_map page numbers verified.
All seven packet limitations are present and faithful to the packet wording (limitations_map verified).

findings.location: Section 3.4, 'Reading errors are up to about .02 on rates'
findings.finding: Wrong for the coverage figures. results/digitized_rates.csv: rejection-rate points (1,502 read) have reading error at most 0.021, but coverage points (1,813 read) have median 0.031 and maximum 0.0527 (Figures 4.31 and 4.35: 0.016-0.053). The paper itself counts coverage among 'the 3,315 directly read rate points' (Section 6.7, p. 15), so '.02 on rates' understates the measurement uncertainty of more than half the readings and of the coverage line/bar cross-check tolerances (898 of 902). Should-fix that makes an uncertainty number wrong.
Repeats 'Figures 4.17-4.38 were read from images, with reading errors up to about .02 on rates' (inherited from packet limitations[2]); same error as Section 3.4.
Claim-specific limits (H3 image reading 0.0091 at cutoffs 2-3; H4 tentative; S1 zero-estimate pattern; S5 divisor) present and faithful.
Separates Chen's model, design and published numbers from our six contributions, each labeled (our simulation; our calculation with her code; our reading of her figures; thresholds we supplied).

Distinguishes the exact R replay (datasets and point estimates of her printed code) from the Python run (all interval-based results, our seeds), and states the replay is not her published runs. The literal check scope (635 of 1,270 datasets of her first block, RNG state identical after it; r-reproduction/out-full/literal_check.txt) is stated; 'exactly' for all 1,280,000 rests on verbatim code + seeds + that check, which the paragraph and Table 2 disclose. Not overstated.
Assumptions we supplied (population values, numeric readings of words, averaging, scalar summaries, E4 tolerance) are separated from source statements.

'biased direct-effect estimates' matches PDF p. 102 Table 4.8 (PNDE/TNDE 12.50-18.75% within [-.10,.10]) and p. 161 'When bias was present, the measure of bias was a negative value.'; 'cover the true value far too rarely' matches Table 4.9 (PDF p. 138) and p. 164 'systematically fell above the CIs'; 'MINT near zero' matches p. 135 'All power for MINT is near zero.'
'Her tentative minimum of 5,000 cases' matches PDF p. 164 'Tentatively, a minimum sample size of 5000 has accurate Type I error rates and power above .80, regardless of cutoff score.'

S9 opposite-significance conclusion matches PDF p. 157 (printed p. 143); 10 of 15 confirmed from source-values/table_4_7.csv. Source metadata (author, year, title, institution, Digital Commons URL, 203 pages, SHA-256 9206b3d8...e557, 6,720,692 bytes) verified against source/chen2021.pdf.
Defines each estimand against its null (E4 minus nominal .05), units (percentage points; rejection rate), positive meaning, tolerances and basis, and 'Descriptive point estimates; not equivalence.'

Tolerance derivation verified: per-point reading errors .0052 (cutoff 2) and .0131 (cutoff 3), mean .00915, rounded down to .0091; not rounded up to change a label; disclosed as chosen after results (Section 7.5, p. 18). Cutoff-1 point is status 'occluded' and correctly excluded.

Magnitude ratios checked: 43.62/0.04 about 1,000 ('three orders'), 47.07/0.33 about 143 ('two'), 0.0127/0.0091 = 1.40 ('about 1.4 reading errors'); MC SE about .007 for a rate near .05 and about .002 for the 32-cell E4 mean (computed 0.00199).
Polish: 'same direction' for ours 0.04 rests on a rounding tolerance below our own MC SE (0.005-0.019); correct per contract and disclosed in Section 1.

Published 'PNDE and TNDE within [-.10, .10] in only 12.50-18.75% of conditions, with negative bias' = Table 4.8 (PDF p. 102) and p. 161 excerpt. Ours 'within [-.05, .05] in 100% ...; largest |bias| 0.016' = results/table48_ours.csv (max 0.0155) and results/summary.json overall_max_abs_bias 0.01551.

Published 'Coverage 24.10-83.99% ...; true value usually above the CI' = Table 4.9 min/max (PDF p. 138). Ours '94.6-95.6% ...; misses on both sides at similar rates' = results/table49_ours.csv 94.59-95.63, below 1.84-2.71, above 2.52-2.90.
Published 'above 14.08-75.55%, below 0.34-1.93%' = Table 4.9 columns; Ours 'above 2.5-2.9%, below 1.8-2.7%' = table49_ours.csv. Row-level findings in the packet match the rendered cells.

Published 'near zero at every sample size; never reaches .80 (Figure 4.28: 0.057-0.068 in this cell)' = PDF p. 135 text and digitized .0571/.0683. Ours '0.852 at n = 500 for ah = .20 at cutoffs 2-3 (0.836 over all cutoffs); at least .97 for ah >= .13 from n = 1,000' = cells.csv (0.8518; 0.8361) and summary.json (0.9735 minimum at n=1000, ah=.1326).

Published quotes the p. 164 recommendation with 'Tentative'; Ours 86.3% / 89.2%, cutoff ranges 85.7-87.0 / 88.3-89.9 and both-zero conservatism = results/statement_checks.csv n=5000 rows and disagreement_tests.json n5000 (.0015-.0020).

H4 is a tentative grid-wide recommendation (PDF p. 164); classifying it nonscalar (packet comparison_kind nonscalar, contrast_not_applicable) is supported by the source wording: no single signed contrast represents it. The row shows 'qualitative, no scalar contrast', magnitude/direction 'not established', tolerance 'not applicable', while the scientific verdict 'partial' is kept separate.
The full component evidence (shares by n 70.0-89.6% and 35.9-91.4%, by cutoff at n=5,000, exceptions) is retained; no pooled scalar margin invented.
The 'not equivalence' note is stated with the scalar rows; E5's 'not applicable' tolerance makes clear it does not apply to the qualitative claim.
